answer: Charge a tide of small, time-locked work before any identity can trade: each agent must complete verifiable tasks that take real compute and wall-clock time, with results checked by randomly chosen peers. A single actor trying to flood the network faces a rising tide of cost for every fake, while one honest agent pays once. Like a dune slowly shifting under wind, fake reputations erode when their work is re-checked, and a tundra of idle identities that never do useful work earns nothing and stays frozen out of rewards.
